bullets: Game 2 of 6 in a single-deck session ("NERF the Hog Rider NOW!!!"), video 280.4s-556.6s; the eight cards are the video-level list with evolution slots on Cannon and Firecracker ("evo cannon", "evo firecracker"). The eighth slot is Earthquake: the perception pipeline's consensus reads it as Heal Spirit, but that rests only on ~0.5-confidence HUD hand reads, while five Earthquake deploy labels — two of them on the opponent's half, where only Ryley can place — are narrated by him in the first person.

Piloted as a pure cycle deck: nine Hog Riders in 276 s of readable play, at the right bridge (16, 14) five times, the left bridge (1, 15) once and down the middle (10, 14) / (9, 15) twice, with Cannon, Skeletons, Electro Spirit and The Log recycling underneath. His stated case for the plan at clock 1:34: "hog rider gets so many hits throughout the game if you really think about it. Against most of these decks, you're almost always able to get damage."

Defence is the Cannon plus one cheap card, and in the hardest overtime pushes two Cannons at once — one low at (6, 7) to hold the tank, one at (9, 13) to eat Zappies (overtime 1:56-1:47). He cycles toward the evolved Cannon on purpose: "we have to cycle to our evo cannon if we want to be able to defend this" (477-479s).

Mighty Miner is used offensively at the bridge (15, 15) against the opponent's Heroic Bowler and as a bait for the Hog lane (clock 1:25, 0:44), and defensively deep at (5, 10) / (15, 13) / (7, 14) / (15, 12); the ability is popped on the opening drop purely to force a response (302s).

The deck survived a first-minute collapse — own left tower 4786 -> roughly 1000 between clock 2:12 and 2:00 against a Giant/Bowler push — and still won in overtime by chipping the enemy right tower 4858 -> 118 one Hog per cycle, the last damage coming from a Hog + Evo Firecracker push at overtime 1:22 and a spell at overtime 0:24: "Oh my god, I think we got it. Yes. Let's go. What a comeback, man" (547-551s).

Earthquake is the deck's only spell besides The Log and does double duty: three defensive casts on his own half at clock 1:07, overtime 1:38 and overtime 1:08 against the opponent's ground swarm and Zappies ("just earthquake here on defense", 474s), and two offensive casts at (12, 20) at overtime 0:53 and 0:24, the last of which finishes the game as the enemy right tower goes 424 -> 118.

new_deck.rationale: 2.6 average elixir, a single 4-cost win condition sent every cycle, and a 3-elixir building plus Skeletons, Electro Spirit and two cheap spells doing all of the defending.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The list is the standard Hog Earthquake / Mighty Miner / Evo Cannon cycle shell with The Log in the Barbarian Barrel slot, and it wins by out-cycling rather than out-trading: nine Hog Riders went in during 276 s of readable play, and Ryley's stated premise is that "hog rider gets so many hits throughout the game... against most of these decks, you're almost always able to get damage" (358-364s). Defence is cheap and repeatable — Cannon plus Skeletons, Electro Spirit, Firecracker or a defensive Earthquake on the swarm — which lets him hold a beatdown Giant/Bowler push while still affording a Hog on the next rotation, and in a long overtime he can have two Cannons on the field at once. Mighty Miner is the flexible piece: at the bridge it deletes or baits the opponent's biggest defensive troop, at home it blocks a lane, and its 1-elixir ability makes it a forcing move on the opening drop. The weakness the match shows is that nothing in the deck stops a committed tank push cheaply, so the first minute can cost most of a tower before the cycle advantage starts to tell.
